name: Evil-WinRM
what: A Ruby WinRM shell aimed at authorized pentests. It gives an interactive PowerShell-style session over Windows Remote Management, with upload/download, pass-the-hash, Kerberos tickets and in-memory script loading.
when: When WinRM (often TCP 5985/5986) is in scope and you already have valid credentials or a hash/ticket for a Windows host you are allowed to administer during the test.
example: Install the gem on the assessment host: `gem install evil-winrm`.
Open a session to an approved host with a password: `evil-winrm -i 10.10.20.15 -u analyst -p 'REDACTED'`.
Or pass-the-hash when that technique is in the rules of engagement: `evil-winrm -i 10.10.20.15 -u administrator -H '<NTLM hash>'`.
Use `upload`/`download` for evidence files, keep a session log (`-l`), and close the session when the test step is done.
pitfalls: Authors require authorized testing or nonprofit education only; do not point it at systems without written permission.
AMSI bypass and in-memory loaders will be blocked or alerted by modern EDR; agree the technique list with the client.
Kerberos mode needs correct time sync, realm config and usually an FQDN, not a raw IP.
